name: TCA9803DGKR
title: TCA9803 level-translating I2C bus buffer/repeater
summary: A two-channel bidirectional buffer for I2C, SMBus and PMBus that also shifts levels between an A port on 0.8 V to 3.6 V and a B port on 1.65 V to 3.6 V. The B port has a built-in 3.3 mA current source in place of pull-up resistors, and the part buffers without a static voltage offset, so both ports pull down to about 0.2 V. Either supply may be the higher one and they may come up in any order. TCA9803 is the strongest of four family members (0.54, 1.1, 2.2 and 3.3 mA); it drives 400 pF at 400 kHz.
key_figures: 0.04 V typ A side (6 mA); 0.22 V typ B side

circuits.title: Level shifting with the bus master on the A side
circuits.description: A 400 kHz master on a 1.2 V rail talks to a 400 kHz slave on 3.3 V. The master side is the A port: VCCA is 1.2 V and SDAA and SCLA each have a 5 kΩ pull-up to that rail. The slave side is the B port at 3.3 V, wired straight to the slave with no pull-ups, since the internal current source lifts those lines. The master drives EN. The worked example for this circuit has 100 pF on the B side, a 150 ns rise-time target and 400 kHz SCL.

notes: Each supply pin also needs 1 µF and 0.1 µF decoupling placed close to it.
Any TCA980x fits this circuit; with 100 pF and 150 ns at VCCB = 3.3 V the TCA9802 and TCA9803 both qualify, and the TCA9802 is the lower-power choice.

circuits.title: Level shifting with the bus master on the B side
circuits.description: The same translation turned round: the master sits on the B port at 1.65 V and the slave on the A port at 3.3 V, so VCCA is above VCCB. The B lines go straight to the master with no resistors; SDAA and SCLA carry 5 kΩ pull-ups to 3.3 V on the slave side. The master drives EN, whose threshold follows VCCA.

circuits.title: Buffering without level shifting
circuits.description: Master, slave and both supply pins share one 2.5 V rail, so the part only buffers the bus. SDAA and SCLA have 5 kΩ pull-ups to 2.5 V on the master side; the B port runs to the slave with no pull-ups. The master drives EN. The worked example has 200 pF on the B side and a 300 ns rise-time limit at 400 kHz.

circuits.title: Two devices in parallel on one A-side bus
circuits.description: One 1.65 V master bus (bus A) feeds the A ports of two devices, with a single pair of 5 kΩ pull-ups to 1.65 V. U1 translates to bus B at 3.3 V for one slave; U2 runs at 1.65 V on both sides and buffers bus C for a second slave. The B ports each go to their own slave with no pull-ups and are never joined. The master drives each EN on its own line. Worked example: bus B 300 pF, bus C 40 pF, both within 300 ns at 400 kHz.

circuits.title: Pairing with a pass-gate translator on the A side
circuits.description: The master on 1.65 V connects straight to the B port (VCCB = 1.65 V). The A port at 3.3 V, with 5 kΩ pull-ups to 3.3 V, runs into a FET-based pass-gate translator whose far side carries its own 5 kΩ pull-ups to 1.65 V and reaches the slave. Putting the pass-gate on the A side keeps its pull-up current away from the B port. The master's EN output is open drain.

circuits.title: Chaining to a TCA9517 buffer
circuits.description: A 1.65 V master bus with 5 kΩ pull-ups enters the A port. The B port at 3.3 V connects to the A port of a TCA9517 (VCCA = 3.3 V), and the TCA9517's B port at 5 V, with 5 kΩ pull-ups to 5 V, reaches the slave. The TCA9517's A port has an equivalent pull-down resistance below 150 Ω, so it meets the RILC limit on the B port. The master drives EN.

equations.note: The maximum-capacitance curves use the minimum ICS. A slave pin can be taken as 10 pF, the I2C maximum; trace capacitance is found by simulation or from the PCB fabricator's capacitance per length.

operation.text: Each B line is pulled high by an internal current source rather than a resistor. By watching that current the part tells whether an outside device or the part itself holds the line low, so no static voltage offset is needed. The source also speeds the rising edge and keeps supply current low.

Many buffered translators lift their own output low above the input threshold to avoid latching on their own low. This part does not, so the B-side VOL stays low (0.22 V typ) and devices with a fixed VIL threshold see a clean low.

EN is active high with a pull-up of about 250 kΩ to VCCA. Low disables the outputs; high joins SDAA to SDAB and SCLA to SCLB. It can keep a misbehaving slave off the bus at power-up. Change EN only while the bus and the repeater port are idle. EN low does not switch off the B-side current source while VCCB is up.

SDAA and SCLA go high impedance when either supply drops below its UVLO, so traffic can carry on over them with the part unpowered or disabled. The B lines stay pulled up by the current source while only VCCA is low. When VCCB goes below its UVLO the current source shuts off and a weak pull-up resistor holds the B lines so they follow VCCB rather than float. All bus pins block current from flowing back into VCCA or VCCB.
Clock stretching and multi-master arbitration are supported, and overshoot is kept small when control of a line passes between master and slave.

operation.topic: B-side input low: VIL, IILC and RILC
operation.text: A low reaching a B pin is accepted only when the pin is below VIL and the outside device sinks at least IILC (1000 µA min). From an idle bus, pulling the line under VIL already means sinking the whole ICS, so IILC is met. When the A side is held low and the part drives the B side low itself, VIL is already met, and a B-side device must sink IILC before the part treats the low as coming from the B side; this keeps the hand-over during clock stretching or an acknowledge clean. RILC (150 Ω max) is the largest pull-down resistance that can still meet IILC. Series resistance in the B lines adds to it and raises the effective VOL.

IEXT-I is outside current flowing into a B pin from a supply, such as a leaky ESD cell or a pull-up resistor; above 100 µA the minimum IILC no longer holds, and as it grows a device must sink more to send a low. Keep it near zero and fit no B-side pull-ups. IEXT-O is current pulled out of a B pin, such as slave ESD leakage to ground, summed over every device on the line; above 200 µA the part can read it as a low and latch the bus.

operation.topic: What may connect to a B port
operation.text: Not allowed on a B port: any other current source, including another TCA980x's B port, pull-up resistors, current sources or rise-time accelerators; outputs with a static voltage offset, such as the TCA9517's B side; outputs whose pull-down resistance is above 150 Ω. A FET pass-gate translator needs pull-ups on both sides and so belongs on the A port. A TCA9517's A port may go on either port of this part; its B port only on this part's A port. A ports have no such limits and may be joined to each other.

The four parts differ only in ICS. The TCA9803 can be the default, as it drives 400 pF at 400 kHz. To save power, find the B-side load capacitance and rise-time target, read the maximum-capacitance curve for the VCCB in use (a VCCB between 1.65 V and 3.6 V falls proportionally between those two lines), and take the weakest part whose line reaches the target region. A pull-up for the A side is sized as for any I2C bus.

VCCA and VCCB have no sequencing or relative-level requirement: either may rise first and either may be higher, as long as each is in its own range. Fit 0.1 µF and 1 µF decoupling as close as possible to each of the VCCA and VCCB pins.
A DGK layout puts an 0402 capacitor beside the VCCA pin and another beside the VCCB pin, each running to the matching supply plane, with vias to a ground plane at the capacitors and at the GND pin.

Rise and fall times run between 0.3 and 0.7 of the supply on that side. Startup runs from VCCB crossing its maximum UVLO to SDAA/SCLA falling through 0.9 VCCA, with VCCA powered and SDAB/SCLB grounded. Enable and disable times run from EN crossing 0.5 VCCA to SDAB/SCLB passing 0.7 VCCB falling (enable) or 0.3 VCCB rising (disable), with SDAA/SCLA grounded.
